narrative.overview:
This is a developer portfolio presented as a working field notebook: a ruled sheet on a cool paper ground, with graphite text, cobalt annotations, manila index tabs, and stamped statuses. The system is editorial rather than decorative. Its density comes from useful metadata — dates, categories, stack names, plate numbers, page counts — while the reading areas stay open and calm. The page should feel like a document someone actually maintains, not a marketing template dressed as one.

The world refuses the category defaults: no centered hero, no badge row, no equal-card project grid, and no rounded SaaS panels. Work is organized as ledger entries with rules between them, and technical drawings are treated as first-class content. Cobalt is the annotation ink: it marks links, active states, index numbers, and the one action that matters on a screen. It is never a large background wash.

The material palette is warm and low-chroma, with soft paper-lift shadows reserved for raised sheets and hover states. Thin warm-gray rules do most of the structural work. Typography pairs a characterful grotesk display with a readable sans and a mono face reserved for metadata, measurements, and code. Placeholder content is visibly provisional and never dressed as a real client outcome.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground with a faint drafting grid on section headers and technical plates.
Graphite ink for reading, cobalt for annotation and interaction, manila for index tabs.
Ledger rows and ruled sheets instead of card grids and rounded panels.
A 3/9 editorial split with a sticky left margin for section index and context.
A 4:5 profile portrait plate anchors the home hero; the SDLC process map sits below the four process phases.
Mono metadata at small sizes, with generous space around display type.
Soft, offset paper-lift shadows; 1px warm rules are the default separator.

Editable site logo replaces the FA monogram, sits directly on paper, and uses a raised-paper backing on dark auth surfaces. The browser tab icon follows the uploaded logo via a generated 64×64 PNG favicon, with public/favicon.svg as fallback.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is ink, not paint. It appears on links, active states, index numbers, focus rings, and one primary action per screen; it does not fill large sections or become a decorative gradient.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: No pure white and no pure black. Grounds are warm paper, raised surfaces are lighter paper, and reading text is graphite. If a surface needs separation, add a 1px warm rule before adding a shadow.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Status colors are for stamps, inline validation, and small state markers. A red or green surface never becomes the background of a full section.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Metadata Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for code, dates, measurements, statuses, table headers, and short labels. It never sets a paragraph, a project summary, or a marketing sentence.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display and headline tracking never goes looser than -0.025em, and display line-height stays at 0.94. If a heading needs more room, shorten the line or reduce the size; do not loosen the tracking.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: The system has two reading voices: display for statements and Instrument Sans for explanation. Mono is the annotation layer. Do not introduce a third reading face.

rules.name: The Ledger Rule
rules.body: Project work is presented as ruled rows with numbers, stamps, summaries, and plates. It is never an equal-card grid, and no project is promoted with a larger card unless it is a featured entry inside the ledger.

rules.name: The Margin-Note Rule
rules.body: Section index and context live in the left margin, not as a kicker above the heading. The heading starts the reading column; the margin explains where the reader is.

rules.name: The One-Screen Rule
rules.body: Every public screen has one obvious next action. Secondary actions are quieter buttons or text links; they do not compete with the primary action.

rules.name: The Paper-Lift Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, offset, and low-opacity. At rest, a surface is flat unless it is a sheet or a plate; hover may lift it by one step, never by a theatrical jump.

rules.name: The One-Sheet Rule
rules.body: A section gets at most one raised sheet. Nested panels use sheet-flat with a 1px border and no shadow, so the hierarchy stays legible.

rules.name: The Ruled-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Every container is defined by a 1px warm rule, a paper fill, or both. If a container needs a border radius larger than 4px, it is probably the wrong component.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Technical drawings are framed as plates: 1px border, paper-deep ground, plate number, category label, and a bottom metadata strip. They are content, not decoration.

dos: Do keep the page on Cool Paper and use Raised Paper only for sheets, fields, and plates.
Do use Annotation Cobalt for links, active states, index numbers, focus rings, and one primary action per screen.
Do set section context in the 3-column left margin and start the heading in the reading column.
Do use 1px warm rules as the default separator; reach for a shadow only when a sheet or plate needs lift.
Do set mono labels at 0.6875rem or smaller with 0.14em tracking, and keep paragraphs in Instrument Sans.
Do keep the drafting grid faint (4.5% ink) and use it on section headers and plates, not behind long-form body copy.
Do label placeholder projects with the “Contoh” stamp and keep their copy explicitly provisional.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion by collapsing transitions and diagram animations to near-instant.
donts: Don't use pure white or pure black; the palette is paper and graphite.
Don't turn the project index into an equal-card grid or a gallery of screenshots.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow directly above a heading; use the left margin or a metadata strip instead.
Don't use a colored left border thicker than 1px on cards, callouts, alerts, or list items.
Don't fill large sections with cobalt, stamp red, or success green; those are annotation and status inks.
Don't use rounded SaaS cards, pills, or radii above 4px for standard containers.
Don't use mono for paragraphs, project summaries, or marketing copy.
Don't invent clients, metrics, testimonials, or outcomes for placeholder projects.
